title: Aperiodic 16-layer fully-optimized stack
scientific_hypothesis: Free optimization of all 16 layer thicknesses without periodicity constraints can achieve superior spectral shaping compared to periodic designs, exploiting the full design space within the manufacturing limit.
design_principle: Aperiodic multilayer optimization allows independent control of each interface's contribution to the spectral response, enabling custom spectral profiles that periodic structures cannot achieve. More degrees of freedom should enable better trade-offs between LWIR transmission and MWIR suppression.
proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | Ge substrate (16 layers total, 8 alternating pairs, no periodicity constraint on thicknesses)
design_variables: Individual thickness of each of the 16 layers (thickness_1 through thickness_16)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band
Achieve steeper transition between stopband and passband compared to periodic designs
manufacturing_considerations: Maximum 16 layers as specified by user
Aperiodic design requires precise individual layer control
Higher layer count increases total stress and deposition time
ZnS/ZnSe material pair has documented compatibility for IR filters
theory_basis: Numerical optimization of multilayer transfer matrices
expected_advantages: Maximum design freedom within layer count constraint
Potential for superior spectral performance over periodic designs
Can compensate for material dispersion effects through thickness tuning
known_risks: 16 layers may accumulate significant residual stress
Optimization may converge to local minima
Manufacturing tolerance sensitivity increases with layer count
ZnSe resolution depends on local material registry
execution_request_english: Optimize an aperiodic 16-layer multilayer film on Ge (Icenogle) substrate with air incidence. Stack order: Air | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | Ge (Icenogle). Sixteen design variables: thickness_1 through thickness_16, each controlling one layer independently. Wavelength bands: 8000-11000 nm (maximize transmittance), 3000-5000 nm (minimize transmittance). Total layers fixed at 16. Materials: zns, ZnSe (Querry), Ge (Icenogle). Find thickness values that maximize LWIR transmission while suppressing MWIR without periodicity constraints.
